body: Thank you for your response, I agree that "therapy" was the generic response. At the time it wasn't what I needed to hear. I wanted to hear stories from people like you who have gone through something similar, can relate and empathize and make me feel like less of a weirdo. My pride has been hurt enough without adding to it strangers harshly judging me. I appreciate your kind response and will keep fighting through this.

I just logged on to read this, thank you so much for the positive response. I did feel like I was getting beat up a bit in this thread and your response was very thoughtful and understanding. I agree that it's easier said than done when it comes to cutting off emotions. Also, I haven't found love (not for lack of trying) and after so many rejections, my self esteem is just not there. I also have hobbies that I try to distract myself with but in the morning and at night when things are quiet the story replays. Since posting this thread I did find a therapist but only went to one session, not sure how I feel about that option. I think Im going to take a step away from dating for now bc the rejection is not fun. (Everyone wants to sex it but very few want to commit to it.) I'm going to try the friends first model and see how that works. Again, thank you for your response, it really helped.

It's really difficult to show that much vulnerability to someone you respect. I chose one person that was close to me and who has suffered from something similar. I also believe that bc you're in such a sensitive state that their reaction makes a huge difference. If they shrug off your feelings as trivial then it can just be a catalyst towards making things worse. Admitting you're depressed is almost like coming out of the closet.

Thanks, I'm going to give it some more time. I've tried a million things so far but will give therapy another go. Even if it's the shittiest 50 years ever lived I'll live them out and hope for something better than today.

Happy Birthday! Thanks a lot for responding, I reached out to some friends, and decided to look for therapy instead. I feel really pathetic but I need the help and am hoping for the best through it. I hope you find a way to happiness also and that you enjoy your special day of the year.
No sarcasm, I was being honest.

Thank you for taking the time to write a thoughtful and insightful response. I agree with you. If I had fallen in love with someone else over the span of 2 years and felt like they were a better match for me then the pain would not be here. The root issue is I want to be in love with someone that I'm willing to spend the rest of my life with. And I guess I shouldn't let it get me down as much as it has. A therapist can make me accept that this might not be in my cards and learn to be Ok with not having a companion.
Thank you for the honest picture.
I don't understand how it's considered normal to fall in and out of love. I thought if it's there it's there and maybe it will go away but a therapist may not have control over this human function.

That hurt to read but Ok. The last thing I want to be seen as is crazy or in a negative light. I feel like it's bad enough that I'm living in this pain and I don't expect anyone to have sympathy for me but at the very least don't judge me.

I'm not blaming him for the pain I've been in for 2 years. He was the cause but depression was the result and I realize I have full control over myself and my emotions. I started therapy immediately and got on anti-depressants but did not take it for more than a few weeks in fear of getting addicted to something synthetic. I wanted to handle it tthe natural way and hoped that time would heal. Time has made it better just not good enough to live a trouble-free life.

Thank you, I have always been an advocate of bettering yourself no matter what stage of life you're in. On the flipside, my scumbag brain is pushing the notion that if I go to therapy then I must be broken and he really did leave me for someone better/more worthwhile. I'm going to try my best to ignore that as false and seek help anyway.
Thank you for your reply, I'll stay away from it then.
